Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

def run_file(filename):

def parse_expr(tokens, index):
    if index >= len(tokens):
        raise SchemeError("Unexpected end of input")

    token = tokens[index]

    if token == "(":
        index += 1
        elements = []
        while index < len(tokens) and tokens[index] != ")":
            expr, index = parse_expr(tokens, index)
            elements.append(expr)
        if index >= len(tokens):
            raise SchemeError("Missing closing parenthesis")
        index += 1

        result = None
        for i in range(len(elements) - 1, -1, -1):
            result = Pair(elements[i], result)
        return result, index

    elif token == ")":
        raise SchemeError("Unexpected closing parenthesis")

    elif isinstance(token, String):
        return token, index + 1

    elif token == "'":
        expr, index = parse_expr(tokens, index + 1)
        return Pair("quote", Pair(expr, None)), index

    else:
        # Try to parse as number
        try:
            return int(token), index + 1
        except ValueError:

        # Check for boolean literals

            return True, index + 1
        elif token == "#f":

;; eval.scm - a metacircular evaluator for the Scheme-like language
;; implemented by interp.py.
;;
;; Usage:  echo -e 'test/calculator.scm\n(+ 7 8)' | python3 interp.py eval.scm
;; Reads one line (a file path), then interprets that file. Remaining
;; STDIN is left for the interpreted program; output goes to STDOUT.

;;; ---------- small list helpers (not part of the language's builtins) ----------
(define (caar x)   (car (car x)))
(define (cadr x)   (car (cdr x)))
(define (caddr x)  (car (cdr (cdr x))))
(define (cadddr x) (car (cdr (cdr (cdr x)))))
(define (cddr x)   (cdr (cdr x)))

(define (length lst)
  (if (null? lst) 0 (+ 1 (length (cdr lst)))))

(define (list-ref lst i)
  (if (= i 0) (car lst) (list-ref (cdr lst) (- i 1))))

;;; ---------- environments: (parent . bindings-alist) ----------
;; bindings-alist is a list of (name . value) pairs.  #f means "no parent".
(define (assq-bindings alist key)
  (cond
    ((null? alist) #f)
    ((eq? (caar alist) key) (car alist))
    (else (assq-bindings (cdr alist) key))))

(define (env-lookup env name)
  (let loop ((e env))
    (let ((hit (assq-bindings (cdr e) name)))
      (if hit
          (cdr hit)
          (if (eq? (car e) #f)
              (begin (display "Error: unbound variable ")
                     (display name)
                     (newline)
                     #f)
              (loop (car e)))))))

(define (env-define env name value)
  (set-cdr! env (cons (cons name value) (cdr env))))

(define (env-set! env name value)
  (let ((hit (assq-bindings (cdr env) name)))
    (if hit
        (set-car! (cdr hit) value)
        (if (eq? (car env) #f)
            (begin (display "Error: unbound variable in set! ")
                   (display name)
                   (newline)
                   #f)
            (env-set! (car env) name value)))))

;;; ---------- procedures ----------
(define (my-procedure? p)
  (and (pair? p) (symbol? (car p)) (eq? (car p) 'my-procedure)))

(define (make-proc params body defenv)
  (cons 'my-procedure (cons params (cons body defenv))))

;;; ---------- the metacircular evaluator ----------
(define (my-eval expr env)
  (cond
    ((not (pair? expr)) (my-self-eval expr env))
    ((my-procedure? expr) expr)
    (else (my-eval-application expr env))))

(define (my-self-eval expr env)
  (cond
    ((number? expr) expr)        ; numbers (and booleans, which are ints)
    ((string? expr) expr)        ; string objects
    ((null? expr) expr)          ; empty list / #f-ish null
    ((my-procedure? expr) expr)
    ((symbol? expr) (env-lookup env expr))
    (else expr)))                 ; host builtins etc.

(define (my-eval-application expr env)
  (let ((op (car expr))
        (rest (cdr expr)))
    (cond
      ((symbol? op)
        (cond
          ((eq? op 'quote)  (cadr expr))
          ((eq? op 'if)     (my-if expr env))
          ((eq? op 'define) (my-define expr env))
          ((eq? op 'set!)   (my-set! expr env))
          ((eq? op 'lambda) (my-lambda expr env))
          ((eq? op 'let)    (my-let expr env))
          ((or (eq? op 'begin) (eq? op 'progn)) (my-begin expr env))
          ((eq? op 'cond)   (my-cond expr env))
          (else (my-apply (env-lookup env op) (eval-args rest env)))))
      (else
        (my-apply (my-eval op env) (eval-args rest env))))))

(define (eval-args args env)
  (if (null? args)
      '()
      (cons (my-eval (car args) env) (eval-args (cdr args) env))))

(define (my-if expr env)
  (let ((c (my-eval (cadr expr) env)))
    (if (eq? c #f)
        (if (< 3 (length expr)) (my-eval (caddr expr) env) #f)
        (my-eval (caddr expr) env))))

(define (cadr x)   (car (cdr x)))
(define (caddr x)  (car (cdr (cdr x))))
(define (cadddr x) (car (cdr (cdr (cdr x)))))
(define (cddr x)   (cdr (cdr x)))

(define (length lst)
  (if (null? lst) 0 (+ 1 (length (cdr lst)))))

(define (list-ref lst i)
  (if (= i 0) (car lst) (list-ref (cdr lst) (- i 1))))

;;; ---- environments: (parent . bindings-alist) ; #f parent = none ----
(define (assq-bindings alist key)
  (cond
    ((null? alist) #f)
    ((eq? (caar alist) key) (car alist))
    (else (assq-bindings (cdr alist) key))))

(define (env-lookup env name)
  (let loop ((e env))
    (let ((hit (assq-bindings (cdr e) name)))
      (if hit
          (cdr hit)
          (if (eq? (car e) #f) #f (loop (car e)))))))

(define (env-define env name value)
  (set-cdr! env (cons (cons name value) (cdr env))))

(define (env-set! env name value)
  (let ((hit (assq-bindings (cdr env) name)))
    (if hit
        (set-car! (cdr hit) value)
        (if (eq? (car env) #f) #f (env-set! (car env) name value)))))

(define (my-procedure? p)
  (and (pair? p) (symbol? (car p)) (eq? (car p) 'my-procedure)))

(define (my-eval expr env)
  (cond
    ((not (pair? expr)) (my-self-eval expr env))
    ((my-procedure? expr) expr)
    (else (my-eval-application expr env))))

(define (my-self-eval expr env)
  (cond
    ((number? expr) expr)     ; numbers (and booleans, which are ints)
    ((string? expr) expr)     ; string objects
    ((null? expr) expr)       ; empty list
    ((symbol? expr) (env-lookup env expr))
    (else expr)))             ; host builtins and other atoms

          ((eq? op 'quote)  (cadr expr))
          ((eq? op 'if)     (my-if expr env))
          ((eq? op 'define) (my-define expr env))
          ((eq? op 'set!)   (my-set! expr env))
          ((eq? op 'lambda) (my-lambda expr env))
          ((eq? op 'let)    (my-let expr env))
          ((or (eq? op 'begin) (eq? op 'progn)) (my-begin expr env))
          ((eq? op 'cond)   (my-cond expr env))

      (else

    (env-set! env name v)

        (env-define newenv name val)
